solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Late caller's double

parts.note: late in the sense of deceased, no longer living
a caller on the phone is one who rings; the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: Someone who telephoned late turns out to have a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who closely resembles another is that person's double, an exact lookalike.

clue.text: Obscure European film extracts, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the pieces and write what is heard

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, and short excerpts from a film are clips

explanation.surface: A European movie's excerpts are hard to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for E plus CLIPS spoken, 'ee-clips', which is how the answer is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to overshadow or block it out, as the moon blots out the sun.

clue.text: One who's desperate in front of church steps

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman character in the long-running British children's comic The Dandy
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A desperate person stands outside a church before its front steps.
explanation.walkthrough: DESPERATE DAN is a British comic-strip cowboy from The Dandy, so 'One who's desperate' is DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance is a sequence of movements, and steps is a common informal word for one.

clue.text: Call to support popular half of jury, causing offence

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits below the rest

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of jury

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A phone call backs the popular half of a jury, giving offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts RING beneath IN plus JU, the first half of 'jury', as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Injuring means harming or wronging someone, which is causing them offence in the older sense of hurt.

clue.text: Reward for workers in yellow fish?

indicators.note: in says the workers are placed inside the yellow fish phrase

parts.note: golden means yellow, and hake is a fish
hands are manual workers, as in farm hands

explanation.surface: Asks whether a reward for labourers might be a gilded fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow fish' looks like a single creature, but it splits into two words with the workers slipped between them. A golden handshake is a big payment to someone leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish severance payment given to a departing employee is a reward for service.

clue.text: Mislay orders sending back ruling family

indicators.note: back says the run taken from the words is read in reverse
sending here reads as the clue words sending out a run of letters from within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Losing commands means returning the monarchy to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'Mislay' and 'orders'; 'sending back' signals both taking it out and reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a monarch's family are informally called the royals, the reigning dynasty.

clue.text: Firm has one for a hand

indicators.note: has one for a says the letter A gives way to I, the Roman numeral for one

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, as in hold fast

explanation.surface: A company swaps something for a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: FAST with its A replaced by I (one) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand is a fist, and hand can stand for one in boxing slang.

clue.text: Pays for saw, for example, to make some furniture

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
a saw is an example of a tool

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a saw so that furniture can be made.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool for resting the feet is a small item of furniture.

clue.text: Landscape from flats

definitions.meaning: flats are painted wooden frames used as stage backdrops in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: Both the natural view of a place and a theatre's painted backdrop panels share this word.

clue.text: The majority of factory design

indicators.note: the majority of a word drops its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: Most of a factory's layout is on the drawing board.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or drawing worked out in advance, a design.

clue.text: Flag message understood by party

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing
roger is the radio word for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A radio operator signals receipt of a flag at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones pirate banner is a famous flag.

clue.text: Come into sight right by unfinished attraction

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the word for attraction

parts.note: appeal is attraction or charm

explanation.surface: Something emerges when right is set beside a half-formed charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into sight is to become visible, emerge or show up.

clue.text: Employed to finish protecting new tiles

indicators.note: protecting says one piece wraps around and shields the other

parts.note: to end is to finish

indicators.note: new says the letters of tiles are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is taken on to complete a job of guarding fresh tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the tiles into LISTE, and 'protecting' wraps the word for finish around it. 'Employed' is in the sense of engaged for service.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enlisted has been signed up or engaged for service, and so employed.

clue.text: Part of plant put initially in earth for development

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of put
development suggests the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: something placed in soil so it can grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P from 'put'; 'for development' rearranges IN and EARTH (ERIANTH) to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer whorl of a flower, made up of calyx and corolla, is part of a plant.

clue.text: It'll end as problematic but in place

indicators.note: problematic suggests the letters are troubled and set in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone worries a job will end badly, yet it is fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something installed has been fitted and put into position, so it is in place.

clue.text: Vote by working quarry finally producing stone

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of quarry

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: A ballot by those at work at a quarry yields a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony used in jewellery is a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Language heard from all quarters on summit?

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points or quarters
a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: Asks whether talk heard everywhere on a mountaintop is a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts PEAK after the compass points in this down clue. NEWSPEAK is the doublespeak language of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The deceptive official jargon in Orwell's novel is a made-up language.

clue.text: Responsibility? — but it's our treat!

definitions.meaning: a burden or duty that falls on someone
read as two words, said when we are paying the bill

explanation.definitionFit: A duty or burden is one sense; split in two the word says the bill is on us, so we pay.

clue.text: Hurried up to evaluate recount

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, meaning hurried
to rate is to evaluate

explanation.surface: Someone rushed up to assess a fresh count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAN into NAR; 'to' just joins it to RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell it, to relate events.

clue.text: Wanting to cross lake is annoying

indicators.note: to cross here means the first word straddles the second, holding it inside

parts.note: needing means lacking or wanting
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Being made to walk across a lake is irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means provoking or irritating with persistent jibes.

clue.text: At the moment, present is not to be found!

parts.note: now means at the present moment
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Something there a moment ago has now gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nowhere is in no place at all, so it cannot be found.

clue.text: Innocent butcher with no time gets worried

indicators.note: worried suggests the remaining letters are disturbed and rearranged
with no says a letter is taken away from the word

explanation.surface: A butcher who has run out of time grows anxious and claims innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes T from BUTCHER, leaving BUCHER; 'gets worried' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic child, so the word names an innocent.

clue.text: Source of roughage eaten by fruit advocates

indicators.note: eaten by says the first piece goes inside the fruit, as if swallowed

parts.note: peaches are fruit

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of roughage

explanation.surface: A dietitian eats fibre with fruit and champions it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preaches a cause urges or advocates it.

clue.text: Lie about being inexperienced in the origins of Scottish premier league

indicators.note: in says the inexperienced word sits inside the initials
the origins of takes the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: raw means green or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A rookie in Scottish football's top division lounges about.
explanation.walkthrough: SPL, the Scottish Premier League, was the top Scottish football division.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to lie or lounge with limbs spread out carelessly.

clue.text: Shelled crab has it on a dish with curry

indicators.note: shelled strips off the outer letters of crab, leaving its middle

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crab with its shell removed is placed on a plate alongside a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' leaves RA from 'crab'; 'has' and 'on' join it, IT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt with cucumber is served as a cooling side to a curry.

clue.text: Custom-built model with 24 changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters are shuffled into another order

parts.note: 24 refers to the answer at 24 down, a yoghurt side dish

explanation.surface: A model is altered with a cross-reference into something bespoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' mixes MODEL with RAITA, the answer to 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to a client's exact measurements is bespoke or custom-built.

clue.text: One case of Brie? Ten from this animal!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: case of takes the outside letters of Brie, the casing around its middle

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Asks whether one box of French cheese might come from this beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild mountain goat with large curved horns is the animal meant.

clue.text: Tried to lose a crowd

indicators.note: to lose says a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a case that is tried in court is heard

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to give a crowd the slip.
explanation.walkthrough: A case 'tried' in court is HEARD; 'to lose a' removes its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals or people, a crowd.

clue.text: Pause before putting these heartlessly into fighting mole

parts.note: a break is a pause

indicators.note: into says the trimmed word goes inside the fighting

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle of these, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pause before hurling these into battle with a burrowing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' gives TE from 'these', and 'putting into' places it within the fighting word. A mole is also a harbour wall, not just the burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole in the harbour sense is a stone pier or barrier protecting against waves.
